data.narrative:
Westmag is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Hansen and Jordan Sanders that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector universe comprising one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Given the nascent stage and limited narrow-peer comparables at identical stage and valuation tier, the Peer-Median approach is not applicable—only one same-stage peer exists in the filtered set, falling short of the three-point minimum for reliable triangulation. The Stage-Progression method is therefore the primary analytical tool. Applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to Series A to the $11M total raised proxy yields an implied valuation of $28M.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $23M to $32M, centered on a $28M median. The range reflects reasonable variance around the stage-progression estimate, acknowledging that Seed-stage robotics companies typically see 2.0–3.0x step-ups into growth rounds. Primary valuation uncertainties stem from the thinness of same-stage comparables in this subsector and the absence of publicly disclosed transaction multiples from directly comparable private financings. Investor confidence in the founding team's execution capability and the company's technical differentiation will materially influence placement within this range.
